comments.body: I found no definite defect in the shown diff, but I cannot establish safety from it, so a human should review. The change adds multi-process tensor parallelism with several risks I cannot verify here: (1) NCCL collectives captured inside CUDA graphs and piecewise graphs; (2) the driver/worker lockstep protocol, where any divergence between ranks (a spec-decode step, async fill rows, preemption, abort paths) deadlocks with a 30-day timeout; (3) a worker crash during load leaves the driver blocked forever in collectives; (4) `head_dim` changed from a property to a stored field, so any caller using `dataclasses.replace` to change head counts now keeps a stale `head_dim`. The GPU tests need 2 GPUs and were not run in this review, and the CPU gloo tests only cover the CPU path. Please run the GPU tests and check the failure paths before merging.

comments.body: I found no definite defect, but I can't establish safety for this change. Timestamp handling depends on things I can't see. `iso_ts` and `pipe_ts` use `to_timestamp`, which follows the Spark session timezone. `get_spark` isn't in the diff, so I can't tell whether it pins UTC. `pipe_ts` also assumes the endpoint-logs (pipe) export is in America/New_York. The config comment only says console-copied logs carry laptop-local time, and the console format already carries an explicit GMT offset. If the pipe export is actually UTC, every boot-phase interval in `gold_worker_boot_phases` that mixes formats will be skewed by hours. A human should confirm both points.

The seed joins (`gpu_model == gpu_label`, series by `series_label`) depend on `seeds/*.csv`, which I could not review. The `.select(...)` list could also be ambiguous if the bronze runs table already has an `engine` or `gpu_model` column. None of the new silver or gold modules has tests, and the only test file shown covers landing. Please verify against real data.

comments.body: serve_command builds a `pagedserve.cli serve` command line, and nothing in this diff or its tests runs it against the real CLI. The test only checks the strings it builds. I could not see pagedserve/cli.py, so I cannot confirm the flags exist with these names and semantics: --served-model-name, --enable-cuda-graphs, --enable-prefix-caching, --quantization, --tensor-parallel-size, --attn-backend, --block-size, --max-num-seqs and --dtype. The old handler said the CLI runs CUDA graphs by default. If so, `CUDA_GRAPHS=0` would only omit an enable flag and would not disable graphs. A wrong flag makes the worker exit at startup, and the failure only shows up in a deployed GPU image. A human should check against cli.py, or add a test that parses this command with the real argparse parser.

    main = _load('main')
    cmd = main.serve_command('/models/m')
    parser = cli.build_parser()  # adjust to actual parser factory
    parser.parse_args(cmd[3:])

comments.body: This change enables CUDA-graph capture for paged_triton, and I can't confirm that is safe from the diff. GRAPH_CAPABLE_BACKENDS asserts the Triton decode path reads only static device tensors (meta.context_lens_t and meta.block_tables_nonneg). The diff doesn't show PagedTritonAttentionBackend or attn/cuda_graphs.py. I need to know: (1) whether the graph runner is hard-wired to the flash backend; (2) whether Triton kernels are compiled during warmup rather than inside capture; (3) whether the num_splits=None heuristic and the grid stay fixed across the captured buckets. The scratch-block padding behaviour also depends on the Triton backend honouring it. The kernel's own commit says 'GPU validation pending', and the new GPU tests (test_paged_triton_gpu.py) are the only check of the graph path and have not been run. A human should confirm the graph path and the GPU test results before this auto-deploys.

_tile_for changes the tile size, which affects numerics and register pressure, and is validated only by CPU-interpreter tests. The docstring says the tile always divides block_size. That is not guaranteed for a block_size that is a multiple of 16 but not a power of two, such as 48, where tile=32 would straddle two physical blocks. The shape assertion only requires a multiple of 16. Either assert block_size is a power of two or compute tile as a divisor of block_size.

comments.body: The cohort logic depends on a literal `source == 'pulse_coldstart'`, but the Pulse source string is not visible in this diff. If silver uses a different value, the Sep 23 rows silently fall into `host_unknown`, and the cohort rows no longer reproduce the figures the docstring and report cite (147.5 s). Please confirm the literal against silver and the seed contents.

The left join to `dim_coldstart_run_notes` on (series_label, run_index) will duplicate request rows if the new seed has any duplicate key. The seed `coldstart_run_notes.csv` was not shown, so I could not rule this out. Add a uniqueness check or dedupe on the notes keys before joining.

`jsonable` does not handle `Decimal`, `Row` or dict values, so `json.dumps` raises `TypeError` if any gold column has one of those types. It also maps `-inf` to `"inf"`. The template that consumes this JSON was also not reviewable. Please verify the build end to end.
